items.title: PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 Released!
items.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group announces that the first releasecandidate of PostgreSQL 19 is now available for download. As a releasecandidate, PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 will be mostly identical to the initial release ofPostgreSQL 19, though some more fixes may be applied prior to the generalavailability of PostgreSQL 19.The next scheduled update releasefor supported versions of PostgreSQL, on November 12, 2026, will include a largenumber of fixes. Because of this, the release team decided to include thesefixes in PostgreSQL 19 before its general availability. This means a secondrelease candidate, PostgreSQL 19 RC 2, will be available on the same day as theupdate release.The planned date for the general availability of PostgreSQL 19 isNovember 19, 2026. Please see the "Release Schedule" section for more details.Upgrading to PostgreSQL 19 RC 1To upgrade to PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 from earlier versions of PostgreSQL, you willneed to use a major version upgrade strategy, e.g. pg_upgrade orpg_dump / pg_restore. For more information, please visit the documentationsection on upgrading:https://www.postgresql.org/docs/19/upgrading.htmlChanges Since 19 Beta 4Several bug fixes were applied to PostgreSQL 19 during the Beta 4 period. Theseinclude:Several fixes for REPACK (CONCURRENTLY).Several fixes for pg_plan_advice.Several fixes for new query planner optimizations that rely on whether anexpression can be NULL.Several fixes for the automatic enablement of logical replicationwhen wal_level is set to replica.Fix postgres_fdwstatistics import to run as the owner of the foreign table instead of the userrunning ANALYZE.Several fixes for parallel autovacuum.Fix COPY (query) TO ... (FORMAT json)to use the query's column names, including aliases, as the JSON keys instead ofthe table's column names.For a detailed list of fixes, please visit theopen itemspage.Release ScheduleThis is the first release candidate for PostgreSQL 19. The release team plans toissue a second release candidate, PostgreSQL 19 RC 2, on November 12, 2026.Unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional releasecandidate, PostgreSQL 19 should be made generally available onNovember 19, 2026.For further information please see theBeta Testing page.LinksDownloadBeta Testing InformationPostgreSQL 19 Beta Release NotesPostgreSQL 19 Open IssuesSubmit a BugDonateIf you have corrections or suggestions for this release announcement, please send them to the pgsql-www@lists.postgresql.org public mailing list.
